slot.brief: Mixture of two non-reacting gases in a vessel: given masses and molar masses, find total pressure at a given temperature using partial pressures and PV = nRT.

stem: A $12.3\ \text{L}$ vessel at $300\ \text{K}$ contains $4.0\ \text{g}$ of helium and $14.0\ \text{g}$ of nitrogen. Find the total pressure. Take $R=0.082\ \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, $M(\text{He})=4.0\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $M(\text{N}_2)=28.0\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
solution:
The total number of moles is $n=\frac{4.0}{4.0}+\frac{14.0}{28.0}=1.50\ \text{mol}$. Using the ideal gas equation,
$$P=\frac{nRT}{V}=\frac{(1.50)(0.082)(300)}{12.3}=3.0\ \text{atm}.$$
